panels.title: 🟢  Cluster Overview — who is primary, is everything up?
Who is the Primary?
panels.description: Shows the node currently acting as the PostgreSQL primary (leader). GREEN = there is a leader. If this is blank or red, no primary exists — writes are impossible.

panels.title: PostgreSQL Running
panels.description: Is the PostgreSQL process on DC1 alive and accepting connections? 1 = YES (green). 0 = the process crashed or failed to start.

panels.title: WAL Timeline
panels.description: The current WAL timeline number. Starts at 1 when the cluster is created. Increments by 1 on every failover or promotion. Timeline 3 means there have been 2 failover/switchover events since cluster creation.

panels.title: Cluster has a Leader?
panels.description: Is the cluster 'locked' — meaning a leader exists and holds the DCS lock? LOCKED ✓ (green) = normal. NO LEADER (red) = split-brain risk, no primary elected, writes are down.

panels.title: Restart Pending?
panels.description: Does any node need a restart to apply a PostgreSQL config change? 0 = no restart needed (green). 1 = a config change was applied that requires a restart — plan a maintenance window.

panels.title: Failsafe Mode Active?
panels.description: Failsafe mode prevents the primary from stepping down if it temporarily loses DCS contact (protects against false failovers during network blips). 0 = normal mode. 1 = failsafe is actively protecting the primary — investigate DCS connectivity.

panels.title: 📡  Replication Health — is the replica keeping up?
Replication Lag (seconds)
panels.description: How many seconds behind the replica is from the primary. In a healthy cluster this should be near 0. YELLOW > 10s means the replica is falling behind. RED > 60s means serious replication delay — investigate network or disk I/O on the replica.

panels.title: WAL Lag per Replication Slot (bytes)
panels.description: How many bytes of WAL data the replica has not yet consumed. 0 = fully caught up. A growing number means the replica is not streaming fast enough. If a replica goes offline, this will grow until the slot's WAL is exhausted (then pg_basebackup is needed).

panels.title: Node Roles Over Time
panels.description: Shows each node's role as 1 (active in that role) or 0 (not). A clean failover looks like: Master drops to 0, Replica jumps to 1 simultaneously. The point where Master and Replica lines cross is the exact moment of failover/switchover.

panels.title: Replication Slots — Active?
panels.description: Shows whether each replication slot is actively being consumed by its replica. active=1 (green) = replica is connected and streaming. active=0 (red) = replica is offline — WAL is accumulating on the primary disk.

panels.title: ⚡  Database Activity — what is PostgreSQL doing right now?
Database Size
panels.description: Total on-disk size of each database. Useful for capacity planning and detecting unexpected growth (e.g. large table without autovacuum running).

panels.title: Lock Count by Type
panels.description: Number of locks held in the database by lock mode. A spike in RowExclusiveLock is normal during writes. A spike in AccessExclusiveLock or ShareUpdateExclusiveLock usually indicates DDL or VACUUM FULL — these can block other queries.

panels.title: 🕒  Patroni Internal State — DCS and WAL positions
WAL Write Position (xlog_location)
panels.description: The primary's current WAL write position as a numeric LSN. Increasing = writes are happening. Flat = no write activity.

panels.title: DCS Last Seen (seconds ago)
panels.description: How many seconds ago Patroni successfully communicated with the Raft DCS (Distributed Configuration Store). Should be under 10 seconds. If this grows, Patroni is losing contact with its quorum — a failover risk.
